title: Algebraic transport of unit-normalized site composition and identity
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be small sites in a fixed larger sheaf universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $v:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ be functors whose precomposition functors preserve sheaves of sets. For $w=v,u,uv,\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$, let $L_w$ be the specified inverse image, left adjoint to $P_w(H)=H\circ w$, with unit $\eta^w$, constructed by the comma colimit and sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction]. Assume $L_v,L_u,L_{uv}$ preserve finite limits. Lift these functors to ring sheaves and module sheaves by applying them to operation maps through the canonical finite-product and terminal-object comparisons, with the underlying-sheaf identifications of [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. Module sheaves are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

There is a unique natural isomorphism $\gamma:L_{uv}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_uL_v$ satisfying
$$P_vP_u(\gamma_H)\circ\eta^{uv}_H=P_v(\eta^u_{L_vH})\circ\eta^v_H.$$
Equivalently, for every $W\in\mathcal C$ and $s\in H(W)$, it satisfies $\gamma_H((uv)^{-1}s)=u^{-1}(v^{-1}s)$ in $(L_uL_vH)(uv(W))$, where each inverse-image section is the corresponding unit image. This section equation alone determines the natural isomorphism.

For $i=0,1$ put $L_0=L_{uv}$, $L_1=L_uL_v$, and let $p^i_{A,B}:L_i(A\times B)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_iA\times L_iB$ and $p^i_*:L_i(*)\xrightarrow{\sim}*$ be the canonical comparisons. Then
$$p^1_{A,B}\gamma_{A\times B}=(\gamma_A\times\gamma_B)p^0_{A,B},\qquad p^1_*\gamma_*=p^0_*.$$
For every commutative ring sheaf $R$ on $\mathcal C$, $\gamma_R$ is a ring-sheaf isomorphism. For every $R$-module sheaf $M$, $\gamma_M$ is a natural additive isomorphism semilinear through $\gamma_R$: $\gamma_M(a m)=\gamma_R(a)\gamma_M(m)$ on all local sections. These maps respect zero, one, addition, multiplication and module scalar action.

The identity adjunction unit $\eta^{\mathrm{id}}_H:H\to L_{\mathrm{id}}H$ is an isomorphism for every set sheaf $H$ (identifying $P_{\mathrm{id}}$ with the identity). On commutative ring sheaves it is a ring isomorphism, and for every $R$-module $M$ its component is additive and semilinear through $\eta^{\mathrm{id}}_R$.

proof.text:
On objects, arrows and sections, $P_{uv}=P_vP_u$: both send a sheaf $K$ on $\mathcal E$ to $W\mapsto K(u(v(W)))$ with the same restrictions. The hypothesis that $P_v$ and $P_u$ preserve sheaves therefore also gives this property for $P_{uv}$. Use the specified adjunctions of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction]. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], $L_1=L_uL_v$ is left adjoint to $P_vP_u$, with unit
$$\alpha_H=P_v(\eta^u_{L_vH})\circ\eta^v_H.$$
Its Hom bijection is precisely the two successive adjunction bijections, so this is the unit for the specified adjunctions, without changing either choice.

source.place: Tag 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites, proof; Tag 00WX, lemma-adjoint-sheaves; composite unit expanded using categories.tex Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits, and its dual

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to $L_0=L_{uv}\dashv P_{uv}$ and the adjunction $L_1\dashv P_vP_u$ of step 1, taking the right-adjoint identification to be the identity from that step. It gives a unique natural transformation $\gamma:L_0\to L_1$, which is invertible, with
$$P_vP_u(\gamma_H)\circ\eta^{uv}_H=\alpha_H.$$
This is the required normalization, including uniqueness among natural isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites, proof: both inverse images are left adjoints of the same functor; unit-normalized form expanded by the cited categorical lemma

proof.text: Evaluate the equation of step 2 at $W\in\mathcal C$ and $s\in H(W)$. Its left side is $\gamma_{H,uv(W)}(\eta^{uv}_{H,W}(s))$ and its right side is $\eta^u_{L_vH,v(W)}(\eta^v_{H,W}(s))$. By the definition of inverse-image sections, these are exactly $\gamma_H((uv)^{-1}s)$ and $u^{-1}(v^{-1}s)$. Conversely the section equation for every $W,s$ says that the two component functions of the unit equation agree everywhere. They are thus equal sheaf morphisms, for every $H$, and step 2 gives uniqueness. No generation assertion about sections of $L_0H$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 00VE, lemma-adjoints-u, proof: the forward adjunction map is precomposition with the unit; evaluation of the normalized unit equation

proof.text: Let $\pi_A:A\times B\to A$ and $\pi_B:A\times B\to B$ be the projections. By definition $p^i_{A,B}$ has components $L_i(\pi_A),L_i(\pi_B)$. The two composites in the claimed product equation, followed by projection to $L_1A$, are respectively $L_1(\pi_A)\gamma_{A\times B}$ and $\gamma_A L_0(\pi_A)$, equal by naturality; the projection to $L_1B$ gives the same check. The product universal property proves the equation. Both $p^1_*\gamma_*$ and $p^0_*$ have terminal target, so they agree. The comparisons are invertible by the finite-limit hypotheses, with $L_1$ preserving products and the terminal object by successive application of $L_v$ and $L_u$.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, preceding operation-map discussion; elementary projection and terminal-object calculation

proof.text:
Under the identifications of [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image], a binary operation $o:X\times Y\to Z$ transported by $L_i$ is $o_i=L_i(o)(p^i_{X,Y})^{-1}$, and a constant $e:*\to Z$ becomes $e_i=L_i(e)(p^i_*)^{-1}$. For $i=1$ these are also the iterated transported operations: the composite
$$L_uL_v(X\times Y)\xrightarrow{L_u(p^v_{X,Y})}L_u(L_vX\times L_vY)\xrightarrow{p^u_{L_vX,L_vY}}L_uL_vX\times L_uL_vY$$
has projections $L_uL_v(\pi_X),L_uL_v(\pi_Y)$, hence equals $p^1_{X,Y}$; the terminal comparison is checked by its unique target map. Substitution in the definitions of the iterated operation gives $L_1(o)(p^1)^{-1}$, and similarly for constants. Naturality and step 4 now give
$$\gamma_Zo_0=L_1(o)\gamma_{X\times Y}(p^0)^{-1}=o_1(\gamma_X\times\gamma_Y),\qquad \gamma_Ze_0=e_1.$$
Apply these formulas to addition and multiplication on $R$, and to zero and one. Thus $\gamma_R$ is a unital ring map. Its component is already bijective, so its inverse respects the same operations: substitute the preimages of each pair of sections in these equalities. It is a ring-sheaf isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module, operation-map proof; sites.tex Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi; explicit naturality calculation for ring operations

proof.text:
Use the binary-operation equality in step 5 with $X=Y=Z=M$ and $o=+$, and its constant equality with the zero of $M$. This makes $\gamma_M$ additive. With $X=R,Y=Z=M$ and $o$ the scalar action, the same equality is
$$\gamma_M\,\mathrm{act}_0=\mathrm{act}_1(\gamma_R\times\gamma_M).$$
Evaluating it on an arbitrary pair $(a,m)$ over an arbitrary object of $\mathcal E$ gives $\gamma_M(am)=\gamma_R(a)\gamma_M(m)$ on all local sections. The operation transports and the identification of module morphisms are those of [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]; module addition and scalar action have the meaning of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Invertibility of the underlying components gives the additive inverse isomorphism, semilinear through $\gamma_R^{-1}$. For an $R$-linear sheaf map $f:M\to N$, naturality of $\gamma$ gives $\gamma_N L_0(f)=L_1(f)\gamma_M$. This proves the asserted module naturality.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module: action is the transported operation map; elementary substitution in step 5 and evaluation on local sections

proof.text:
For the identity site functor, $P_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{Id}$ on sheaves. Compare the given $L_{\mathrm{id}}\dashv\mathrm{Id}$ with the identity adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. By [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] there is an isomorphism $c:L_{\mathrm{id}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Id}$ satisfying $c_H\eta^{\mathrm{id}}_H=\mathrm{id}_H$. Since $c_H$ is invertible, $\eta^{\mathrm{id}}_H=c_H^{-1}$, proving the identity-unit assertion without an additional finite-limit hypothesis on $L_{\mathrm{id}}$. For completeness its canonical product comparison is invertible: naturality of $c$ and the two projections gives
$$(c_A\times c_B)p^{\mathrm{id}}_{A,B}=c_{A\times B},$$
and the terminal equation is $p^{\mathrm{id}}_*=c_*$. The maps $c_A,c_B,c_{A\times B},c_*$ are isomorphisms, so these comparisons are isomorphisms too. Thus the operation transports assumed for the identity functor have the required invertible comparisons.

source.place: Tag 00WX, lemma-adjoint-sheaves for the identity functor; categories.tex Tag 0037, definition-adjoint; uniqueness argument as in Tag 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites

proof.text:
Write $\eta=\eta^{\mathrm{id}}$. Naturality with the two projections gives $p^{\mathrm{id}}_{X,Y}\eta_{X\times Y}=\eta_X\times\eta_Y$; the terminal equation is $p^{\mathrm{id}}_*\eta_*=\mathrm{id}_*$. Hence for every binary operation $o:X\times Y\to Z$ and constant $e:*\to Z$,
$$\eta_Zo=L_{\mathrm{id}}(o)\eta_{X\times Y}=o_{\mathrm{id}}(\eta_X\times\eta_Y),\qquad \eta_Ze=L_{\mathrm{id}}(e)\eta_*=e_{\mathrm{id}},$$
using exactly the operation definitions of [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. Apply the first formula to ring addition, multiplication, module addition and the action $R\times M\to M$, and the second to ring zero, one and module zero. They prove that $\eta_R$ is a ring map and $\eta_M$ is additive and semilinear through $\eta_R$ on every section. By step 7 these maps are bijective; substituting preimages in the displayed formulas gives preservation by their inverses as well. Thus $\eta_R$ is a ring isomorphism and the identity module comparison is the claimed natural additive semilinear isomorphism.
